name: Valcom Inc.
old_description: Designed and built in the USA since 1977 and backed by 24/7 support.
about:
Valcom Inc. was founded in 1977 in Roanoke, Virginia, where it remains headquartered. The company began with a focus on helping organizations communicate easily with their people, a mission that has evolved over more than four decades into a broader vision of keeping communities safe, informed, and on schedule.

Valcom designs and develops telecommunication systems, paging solutions, emergency notification platforms, and visual messaging solutions. All hardware is designed and assembled in-house, giving the company direct control over quality and the ability to pivot quickly. Proprietary software platforms such as VEMASS and VEEWS support system reliability and survivability. The company has deployed more than 44,000 K-12 communications systems, including for the Los Angeles Unified School District, the second-largest public school district in the United States.

Valcom serves K-12 and higher education, commercial and industrial facilities, healthcare, corporate campuses, transportation, government and military installations, and retail markets. Its solutions are engineered to integrate with existing infrastructure, and the company provides guidance on grant funding for emergency response upgrades. Customers include school districts, hospitals, and federal agencies.

The company emphasizes that its U.S.-based design and assembly, 24/7 technical support, and scalable architecture differentiate it from competitors. Valcom also allows customers to choose their own installers and integrators, and its grant assistance program helps organizations secure funding for safety improvements.

name: Valentine Enterprises Inc
old_description: Valentine Enterprises specializes in custom powder formulation, blending, and packaging. Combining Scientific Expertise with high-quality manufacturing, Valentine brings your product vision to life.
about:
Valentine Enterprises operates a 400,000-square-foot, company-owned facility in Lawrenceville, Georgia, where it provides contract manufacturing services for powder-based nutritional products.

The company’s core services span product development, ingredient sourcing, validated mixing, and precision packaging. Its formulators and scientists work with brands to create or refine powder supplements, including protein powders, vitamins, and nutritional blends. Manufacturing follows straight-line precision processes under cGMP and HACCP standards, with allergen-controlled protocols and rigorous cleaning procedures. The facility supports turnkey projects that manage development, sourcing, production, and quality assurance from concept to finished goods.

Valentine serves brands in the dietary supplement, sports nutrition, and wellness markets. Its client base includes Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies as well as large protein-powder sellers. The company emphasizes proprietary, customer-specific formulations rather than private-label offerings, though it notes it is exploring private-label solutions.

Valentine differentiates itself through a set of core values that prioritize personal quality ownership, ethical decision-making, rapid response times, and commitment adherence. It also highlights its certification portfolio—NSF, cGMP, Organic, Kosher, HACCP, and FDA registration—as evidence of going beyond industry standards. Flavor development is cited as a particular passion and specialty.

old_description: Serving North Central Illinois since 1973.  Our experience in Industrial Fabrication is unmatched.
about:
Valley Fabrication, Inc. was founded in 1973 in La Salle, Illinois. The company operates as a sister concern to Machinery Maintenance, Inc. and On Site Repair Services, Inc., serving Central Illinois from its La Salle base.

The shop provides full-service metal fabrication, including custom weldments, tank and structural steel fabrication, transition and ductwork pieces, stairs, platforms, and conveyor replacement parts. An in-house American Welding Society (AWS) certified training facility runs an apprenticeship program led by a certified instructor.

Valley Fabrication primarily serves industrial maintenance and heavy-equipment sectors in North Central Illinois, repairing buckets, cutting edges, bores, shafts, and wear surfaces for loaders, excavators, dozers, and shovels, as well as screw conveyor flighting, crushers, screeners, and shakers. Its customer base spans cities such as LaSalle, Peru, Ottawa, Spring Valley, Rockford, and Bloomington.

The company emphasizes an AWS-certified workforce, ongoing OSHA safety training, and a mission to deliver the highest value materials and services in the most timely manner. Its apprenticeship program and certified weld inspections are cited as key differentiators.

old_description: A Trusted Wholesale Auto Parts Supplier Serving Southeast Michigan Since 1997
about:
Value Plus Auto Parts Wholesale operates from two locations in the Detroit metro area — Westland and Detroit, Michigan — and has served Southeast Michigan since its founding in 1997. The business was established as a wholesale auto parts supplier focused on repair facilities, commercial auto businesses, and retail customers, building a reputation for dependable service and competitive pricing over more than two decades.

The company distributes a broad range of automotive components including brake parts, ignition components, engine parts, cooling system parts, suspension parts, filters, electrical components, and motor oil for both domestic and import vehicles.

Primary customers are independent repair shops, commercial fleet operators, and retail motorists throughout Southeast Michigan. The supplier also works with independent mechanics and automotive service centers that rely on quick access to quality parts from brands such as Bosch, Denso, Dorman, AC Delco, Timken, TRW, and Hitachi.

Value Plus differentiates itself through a mission to provide quality parts at the most competitive prices by leveraging a network of small businesses that negotiate collectively with vendors. Its promise emphasizes availability, service programs for both retail and repair facilities, and a commitment to longevity through prosperity, backed by knowledgeable staff and a professional, organized operation.

name: VanTran Transformers
old_description: Custom distribution-class transformer manufacturer headquartered and manufacturing in Waco, Texas, now part of the Forgent power infrastructure group.
about:
VanTran Transformers was founded in 1963 in Vandalia, Illinois, and relocated to Waco, Texas in 1974, where it remains headquartered and operates its manufacturing facility. The company is now part of the Forgent power infrastructure group, which combines VanTran with MGM Transformers, States Manufacturing, and PwrQ to deliver end-to-end power solutions.

VanTran designs and manufactures custom distribution-class transformers, including padmount, substation, multi-tap substation, auto-transformers, submersible and vault, grounding, polemount, and dry medium-voltage units (VPI and cast resin). Its capabilities span custom engineering, retrofit design solutions, and in-house manufacturing, supported by a workforce of 51 to 200 employees.

The company serves industrial, oil and gas, petrochemical, utility, data center, rental power, renewable energy, mining, and transit markets. Customers include data centers, manufacturing facilities, and power-grid operators requiring short delivery cycles and on-time delivery for critical infrastructure projects.

VanTran emphasizes timely, customizable, liquid-filled distribution transformers with what it describes as the shortest lead times in the industry. The firm has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing U.S. companies, citing exponential growth that enables expanded client support while maintaining high-quality standards.

about:
Vaso Corporation, formerly Vasomedical, Inc., is headquartered in Plainview, New York, with additional operations in Wuxi, China; Nashville, Tennessee; and Tampa, Florida. The public company operates across healthcare and information technology through three business units.

The VasoMedical unit designs, manufactures, sells, and services proprietary noninvasive monitoring, diagnostic, and therapeutic devices for cardiovascular disease, with engineering and production centered in its China-based facilities. VasoHealthcare has provided professional sales representation for General Electric Healthcare's diagnostic imaging modalities since 2010, targeting independent hospitals, imaging centers, and multispecialty clinics across the continental United States. VasoTechnology delivers managed IT systems, healthcare software solutions, and secure network connectivity services for enterprise and clinical customers.

The company serves the healthcare sector's middle market, including independent hospitals, imaging centers, and multispecialty clinics for imaging equipment sales, while its medical device unit reaches global markets through direct and partner channels. VasoTechnology supports enterprises and healthcare organizations with mission-critical applications, data storage, and security services.

Vaso Corporation emphasizes its cross-disciplinary expertise spanning medical devices, diagnostic imaging sales, and IT infrastructure, allowing it to address diverse clinical and enterprise needs.

name: Vaughan-Bassett Furniture
old_description: Vaughan-Bassett, the largest manufacturer of wooden residential furniture in the United States, is committed to their hometown of Galax, Virginia, just like we are committed to our hometown of Laurel, Mississippi.  We’ve partnered to create a cottage-inspired furniture line crafted by 600 American workers.  LMCo Bedroom Collections are now available in stores across the United States.
about:
Vaughan-Bassett Furniture has operated from Galax, Virginia, since its founding in 1919 by B.C. Vaughan and J.D. Bassett, Sr. What began as a small regional furniture company grew into the largest manufacturer of wooden adult bedroom furniture in the United States, remaining under the leadership of the Bassett family with John D. Bassett III serving as chairman.

The company employs more than 500 skilled artisans at its Galax factory, where they produce bedroom collections — including Dovetail, Tide & Timber, Cool Rustic, Bonanza, Pure Maple, and Maple Road — using wood solids and veneers such as oak, maple, cherry, ash, poplar, birch, beech, and pine. Modern manufacturing technology complements traditional craftsmanship, and the firm reports that 99 percent of its materials are sourced domestically.

Vaughan-Bassett sells through a dealer network to residential customers across the country. Its furniture is designed for real homes, meeting federal stability requirements under 16 CFR Part 1261 (ASTM F2057) for clothing storage units, and the company is a member of the American Home Furnishings Alliance.

The company's differentiation rests on a deliberate choice to keep production in America when much of the industry moved overseas. That commitment is documented in the bestselling book Factory Man. Vaughan-Bassett also operates a One for One sustainability program that has contributed more than six million tree seedlings to the Virginia Department of Forestry, and it sources 99 percent of its lumber within 500 miles of its factories.

name: Vault Foods
old_description: The U.S. FDA has approved Vault Foods™ solution as a processing aid, which means that it is so safe to use that labeling is not required.
about:
Vault Foods operates from its headquarters in Fair Oaks, Texas, with an SQF-certified treatment facility in Boerne, Texas. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides a food safety treatment service that uses an FDA-approved organic processing aid to reduce pathogens on foods such as nuts, seeds, and other packaged products. At its Boerne facility, the Neo-Pure system—developed in partnership with Agri-Neo—mists a proprietary biodegradable solution onto food surfaces and crevices, achieving a validated 5-log (≥99.999%) reduction of Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria without heat, irradiation, or chemical gases. The process preserves the food's raw taste, smell, texture, and nutrition, and the solution biodegrades completely, leaving no residue and requiring no label declaration.

Vault Foods serves food processors and manufacturers in the nut, seed, and packaged-food sectors who need to extend shelf life while maintaining a "truly raw" product claim. Its treatment is designed to integrate into existing supply chains, offering certified freshness without altering the natural qualities of the food.

The company emphasizes that its processing aid is so safe the FDA does not require labeling, and that the organic, biodegradable solution differentiates it from thermal or chemical alternatives. The service was created to give food brands a way to achieve high-level pathogen reduction while keeping products raw and organic-compliant.

about:
Venture Medical ReQuip, Inc. is a family-owned medical equipment dealer based in Tampa, Florida. The business traces its roots to the mid-1980s when John Pritchard Sr., a firefighter, purchased a piece of medical equipment at a local auction and resold it for a profit. That single transaction grew into a company that has been family owned and operated since 1985, remaining independent of private equity or outside investors.

Today the company operates from an 18,000‑square‑foot facility in Tampa and maintains an online catalog of roughly 1,587 products across more than 30 categories. It supplies new, refurbished, and used medical equipment — including surgical tables, stretchers, patient monitors, defibrillators, infusion pumps, and OR stainless steel — and provides on‑site biomedical testing and repair services throughout the Tampa Bay area. Venture Medical also offers turn‑key ambulatory surgical center setups, short‑ and long‑term equipment rentals, and volume pricing for dealers, with every product shipping nationwide under a standard warranty.

The customer base spans ambulatory surgical centers, hospitals, and medical offices across the United States. Testimonials cite surgeons and facility directors in New Jersey and Florida who have relied on the company for everything from single‑item purchases to complete facility build‑outs.

Venture Medical says its differentiation lies in its family‑run values — honesty, integrity, and value — and its commitment to setting a benchmark for how pre‑owned equipment should be refurbished. The leadership emphasizes that independence from outside capital allows decisions focused on patient and staff safety rather than earnings pressure.

about:
Founded in 1998 in Stowe, Vermont, Vermont Electronics began as a technology services firm serving the Stowe area and broader Vermont region.

The firm specializes in custom design and installation of integrated audio/video, home theater, smart home automation, lighting control, and security systems for both residential and commercial settings. Services encompass whole-house audio distribution, remote and mobile access for heating, security, and lighting, and coordination with new construction or renovation projects. old_description: Our fabricators can do just about anything!  We have been providing quality service in Fredericksburg since 1950.
about:
Viking Steel Fabricators began in 1950 as the Fredericksburg Machine Shop in downtown Fredericksburg, Virginia. After moving to its current Airport Avenue location beside the city fairgrounds in the 1970s, the shop was purchased by Clayton Mills from his uncle Mr. Stoner. In 1985 Mills hired Don Breivik to start a steel fabrication division; Breivik bought the business in 1999, renaming it Fredericksburg Machine & Steel and expanding to 13 employees. Ownership passed to Don's sons Luke and Erik in 2016, with Luke becoming sole owner in 2017. The 2019 acquisition of Virginia Architectural Metals added ornamental iron and historic restoration capabilities. The company remains family‑operated, with Luke Breivik as president and multiple relatives on staff.

The firm fabricates and erects structural and miscellaneous steel for commercial, institutional, and residential projects throughout Virginia, Washington, D.C., and Maryland. Services include shop and field welding, plate shearing, plate bending and rolling, pipe threading, plasma cutting, and custom handrails in carbon steel, aluminum, stainless steel, bronze, brass, and wrought iron. Viking also stocks steel shapes, plate, pipe, tubing, bar grating, and expanded metal for sale. A 13‑person crew works from the Airport Avenue facility, handling jobs from ornamental railings to large structural packages.

Completed projects span the Antietam Battlefield Tower (Maryland), the Admiral Club and the Pentagon (D.C. area), Virginia Railway Express stations, the Orange County Public Safety Building, the Eastern Shore Public Library, and a satellite dish mount in Greenland. Customers include general contractors, developers, government agencies, healthcare providers such as Patient First, and retailers like AAA. The historic preservation niche, strengthened by the Virginia Architectural Metals acquisition, targets restoration of landmark structures.

Viking highlights its 70‑plus years in Fredericksburg, mobile welding service, and a full steel inventory as differentiators. The 2019 closure of the machine shop to concentrate solely on fabrication reflects a strategic response to sustained demand for structural and ornamental metalwork, supported by the expertise of former Virginia Architectural Metals owners Mike and Betsy Rodrigue.

about:
Walco Electric Co. opened in 1931 in Providence, Rhode Island, when founder Edmund Waldman began manufacturing radio antenna kits before pivoting to electric motor repair for the region’s wire and textile mills. The shop grew alongside the port of Providence into one of the Northeast’s largest electrical apparatus service facilities, adding a maintenance machine shop, electrical contracting, and an electronic motor control group over the next four decades.

Today Walco operates through three groups: Automation and Controls, which provides systems engineering, drive integration, and motion control as a Siemens Solution Partner with more than 1,500 drives installed worldwide; Industrial Power Systems, delivering electrical and mechanical maintenance, repair, and on‑site service; and Rail Transportation, which rebuilds, rewinds, and remanufactures AC and DC traction motors, generators, and auxiliary equipment at what the company calls New England’s largest transit motor rebuilding facility, staffed by over 40 technicians working three shifts with 24/7 emergency coverage.

The rail group serves mass‑transit agencies and Class I railroads, including the MBTA, SEPTA, Metro‑North, New York City Transit, and the Cleveland, Pittsburgh, and Baltimore authorities. Automation and Controls customers span metals, paper, plastics, converting, textiles, and roofing industries, while Industrial Power Systems supports national and international industrial plants.

Walco traces its differentiation to a founding emphasis on integrity and customer service, encapsulated in the slogan “Never Underestimate the Power of Total Commitment,” and highlights its AAR M‑1003 certification, ISO‑compliant quality program, and status as the only Siemens motion partner in the Northeast.

Watersong Custom Furniture operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where owner Andy has run the business as a sole proprietor for over four decades. Watersong serves homeowners and individual clients seeking custom pieces that fit unique spaces and functional needs. Examples from the portfolio include a low maple table for a meditation room, a built‑in vanity with dual sinks and a cedar‑lined hamper, and entertainment centers designed to adapt to evolving technology.

Andy emphasizes that the sole‑proprietor model ensures a single point of accountability from design through delivery, eliminating the “too many cooks” problem. The company’s differentiators are its four‑decade tenure at one address, hand‑selected materials, premium hardware, and a willingness to ship finished pieces across the country—from Wyoming to Texas and California to New Jersey.

Waxoyl USA operates from Westford, Vermont, where it was founded in 1971. The company specializes in corrosion protection solutions for transportation, machinery, and structures, drawing on more than five decades of experience in the field.

The product line centers on three main coatings: Hardwax, a tough, flexible wax-based barrier for underbody protection; Professional 120-4, a cavity fogging treatment that penetrates seams and displaces moisture; and Hardwax21, formulated for maximum abrasion resistance in extreme environments. All products are supplied in kegs, tins, and aerosol cans alongside a range of professional application tools designed to reach cavities without drilling.

The coatings are used by original equipment manufacturers across automotive, commercial vehicle, and rail sectors, including car, bus, and truck makers, vehicle importers, pre-delivery inspection centers, train builders, and heavy earth-moving equipment producers. Specialists worldwide apply the system to protect bridges, fleet vehicles, and industrial structures.

Waxoyl emphasizes that a single application of 120-4 can protect for the life of a vehicle, with active protection spanning -40°F to 300°F. The coatings are safe on paint, rubber, and electrical components, and they stop existing surface rust while lubricating moving parts such as window tracks. Touch-ups are needed only where the coating has been physically abraded.

name: White Lightning - Aviation Ground Power
old_description: From our years of building high current DC power supplies for demonstrating mobile electronics and our continuous involvement in general aviation since 1980, comes our line of Ground Power Units to safely power cockpit and airframe systems with clean, stable airframe power. We also distribute the aviation-specific BatteryMINDer® and provide wiring kits for FAA-certified aircraft to simplify installation and increase safety.
about:
White Lightning Aviation Ground Power is based in Lexington, Kentucky. The company traces its roots to the 1980s when founder Jon Sisk, a longtime pilot, began building high-current DC power supplies for mobile electronics demonstrations. Recognizing a need for reliable, affordable ground power units in general aviation, Sisk and his engineering team developed the first Enhanced Flight GPU, establishing the company's focus on airframe ground power.

The company designs and manufactures a line of ground power units (GPUs) covering 14 V, 28 V, and dual‑voltage configurations, including smart GPUs with integrated battery‑maintenance chargers. It also produces aviation‑grade power cables, wiring harnesses, and plug assemblies, and distributes the BatteryMINDer® line of charger‑maintainers. All manufacturing is done in the United States, with product models such as the M2875‑114 (114 A, 28 V), M2827 (27 A, 24/28 V), M1428‑DV (dual‑voltage mini), M2850 (50 A, 28 V), and several 14 V variants for certified and experimental aircraft.

Its equipment is used to power cockpit avionics — such as Garmin G1000 suites — during preflight, maintenance, database updates, and training without draining the aircraft battery. Customers include owners of certified aircraft like the Cessna Skylane and Piper Navajo, as well as experimental/amateur‑build operators.

The company was started because Jon Sisk saw a gap in affordable, reliable hangar ground power. It differentiates itself by pursuing three principles: sensibly designed, well‑made products at reasonable prices; great customer service with direct phone support; and manufacturing everything possible in the USA.

Whiteside's equipment is used across automotive, heavy-duty, big-truck, industrial, agriculture, refinery, and aerospace sectors. The company has earned multiple "Vendor of the Year" awards from customers for innovation, service, and delivery performance. It also offers custom garage equipment designed to match specific industry standards and requirements.

The founder's original mission—to build the finest garage equipment in the professional tool world—remains the guiding principle. The leadership team, led by CEO Kirt Whiteside and CFO Terry Whiteside, continues to operate on the credo: build it better, build it right, and never settle.

The company stocks a wide range of fuses — glass, ceramic, automotive, thermal, pico, and microwave types — from brands such as Bussmann, Littelfuse, Ferraz Shawmut (Mersen), Daito, Fuji, and SIBA. It also offers capacitor replacement kits for television and monitor power or inverter boards, along with individual capacitors, ICs, semiconductors, resistors, transistors, and diodes. Witonics notes that it is not an authorized distributor for Bussmann, Littelfuse, or Mersen products.

The product catalog spans industrial fuse series and component-level kits for board-level repair.

Witonics emphasizes RoHS-compliant inventory and fast shipping, with customer reviews highlighting quick delivery and responsive service. The capacitor kits target common failure symptoms such as slow startup, flickering screens, clicking noises, and power-LED issues in TVs and monitors.

about:
Woeber Mustard Company has been operating in Springfield, Ohio since its founding in 1905. The family-owned business traces its roots to the Woeber family, with Ray Woeber becoming the face of the brand as the "Mustard Man" in 1945. Over more than a century, the company has remained under family stewardship, building a reputation for condiments produced in its Midwestern facility.

The company manufactures a range of condiments including mustard, horseradish, mayonnaise, vinegar, lemon juice, and various dips. In addition to its branded lines, Woeber offers private-label production for food service and retail partners. All products are made at the Springfield plant, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volumes.

Woeber serves two primary channels: food service operators and retail distributors.

The company attributes its longevity to family pride and a hands-on passion for mustard and horseradish quality. The legacy of the Mustard Man symbolizes a culture of innovation and fun that continues to guide product development today.

old_description: Trusted by Oregon families since 1978 — real hardwood furniture crafted to last generations.
about:
Wood Castle Company Store, based in Albany, Oregon, has been crafting solid wood furniture since its founding in 1978. The family-owned business began with a focus on heirloom-quality pieces built to last generations, serving homeowners throughout the Willamette Valley.

The company manufactures bedroom, dining, occasional, storage, and limited-edition furniture collections using sustainably sourced domestic hardwoods. Its production combines time-tested woodworking techniques — including mortise-and-tenon and dovetail joinery — with precision machinery to achieve tight-fitting components and reinforced construction. The factory operates on hydroelectric power and reports that approximately 99 percent of wood fiber is used or recycled, minimizing waste.

Wood Castle sells directly to residential customers through its Albany showroom and offers local delivery to communities such as Corvallis, Salem, Newport, and Lincoln City. Its furniture is designed for everyday use, with heavy-duty drawer glides and reinforced drawer bottoms intended to ensure long-term reliability.

The business emphasizes longevity over trends, citing a commitment to domestic materials, renewable energy, and construction methods that prioritize repairability and durability. Custom options are available, allowing buyers to tailor pieces to specific spaces.

about:
WoodLab operates from Eagle, Idaho, where it was founded in 2017 as a homegrown woodshop. The company began by crafting custom furniture from locally rescued urban wood, serving the Boise area and the broader Treasure Valley.

The shop handcrafts solid wood and epoxy river tables, custom art pieces, and ready-to-ship furniture. Its processes include live-edge slab selection, epoxy casting in colors such as multi-grey and dolphin grey, and concealed hardware installation that leaves no visible fasteners. An interactive online design tool lets customers specify wood species, epoxy color, leg style, and dimensions for a base price estimate. Finished pieces ship nationwide via LTL freight and internationally.

Customers range from residential buyers to commercial clients outfitting boardrooms and conference rooms. The product line includes dining tables, coffee tables, charcuterie boards, and wall art sculptures. WoodLab serves the Treasure Valley locally while fulfilling orders across the United States and overseas.

The company emphasizes its use of locally rescued urban wood and a hidden-hardware approach as key differentiators. The custom design tool streamlines collaboration, allowing clients to visualize projects before production begins.

name: Woodlore, LLC
old_description: Located in Rockbridge County, Virginia, Woodlore LLC is an environmentally conscious business which salvages local trees that have fallen from storms and urbanization. Instead of harvesting trees, we save dead or diseased trees from being processed into non recyclable products such as firewood, and mill them into natural live edge slabs. We sell local wood and build custom furniture.  Some of our featured products include tables, desks, benches, mantels, countertops and bar tops. These custom pieces display the log’s unique spalting, feathering, ambrosia, voids, inclusions, and knots; and may artistically expose nails, bullets, barbed wire and various other articles lodged in the tree. In addition, portable sawmill services are available for clients who wish to reclaim logs from their property and create their own heirloom furniture. We also offer kiln drying services with our iDRY vacuum kiln.  Our mission is to offer new life to dead trees, and thereby provide customers with organic furnishings and artisan materials. Our philosophy is to care for the environment by crafting furniture with locally salvaged trees.  Woodlore values honesty, integrity, and quality craftsmanship.
about:
Woodlore, LLC operates from Fairfield in Rockbridge County, Virginia. The company was founded on the principle of salvaging local trees that have fallen due to storms or urbanization, rather than harvesting live timber. No founding year or founder names are publicly disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

The company mills salvaged logs into natural live edge slabs and fabricates custom furniture including tables, desks, benches, mantels, countertops, and bar tops. All processing—from log salvage to finishing—occurs under one roof. Woodlore also provides portable sawmill services using a Wood-Mizer LT50 Wide hydraulic sawmill, and kiln drying via an iDRY vacuum kiln with a capacity of 13 feet long by 48 inches wide by 55 inches thick (stickered lumber pile), handling up to 2,000 board feet per cycle. Drying time averages approximately one week per inch of lumber thickness. Facility size, employee count, and annual production volumes are not disclosed.

The company’s stated mission is to give new life to dead trees, providing organic furnishings and artisan materials while caring for the environment. Woodlore emphasizes honesty, integrity, and quality craftsmanship, and differentiates itself by keeping the entire process—from salvage to finished product—in-house, allowing clients to participate in wood selection and design.

about:
Woodworks Studio operates at 2555 S Santa Fe, Unit F2, in Denver, Colorado. The studio has offered woodworking instruction for over two decades, with the lead instructor teaching beginner classes for more than 20 years.

The studio provides woodworking education through beginner, intermediate, private, and intensive workshop formats. Beginner classes cover safe operation of table saws, jointers, planers, miter saws, and routers to build a small table or bookcase, including panel glue-up, basic joinery, and finishing techniques. Intermediate classes are student-directed, allowing participants to design and build projects such as jewelry boxes, butcher blocks, coffee tables, dining tables, bookshelves, and cabinets while learning advanced joinery like mortise-and-tenon and dovetails. Private classes offer guided project work for groups. Intensive week-long workshops focus on basic woodworking and cabinet building in small groups.

Classes serve hobbyists, beginners, and intermediate woodworkers seeking hands-on instruction. Customers include individuals purchasing gift certificates — which never expire and are transferable across any class — as well as those scheduling private or semi-private sessions.

The instructor emphasizes safety, noting no significant injuries in over 20 years of teaching beginner classes. The studio aims to provide quality instruction with no hidden fees for beginner classes, and flexible scheduling for intermediate classes that never expire.

name: WorkbenchRVA
old_description: The Workbench was founded to help everyone express their creativity and think outside the box. We feel children need this more than anyone else. A creative child is a happy, social and intelligent child!
about:
WorkbenchRVA operates as a public woodworking shop in Richmond, Virginia. The business was founded by Dalton, a lifelong woodworker who first discovered the craft in middle school. After working at a cabinet shop under mentor Mike Sibley, owner of Sibley's Custom Cabinetry, Dalton developed the concept for a membership-based facility while completing a college business course with guidance from Professor Dr. James Haug. The venture launched to address the loss of school woodshop programs and the lack of accessible shop space for children and adults alike.

The facility provides 24/7 access to a fully operational cabinet shop equipped with table saws, jointers, and planers. Members receive project storage, discounted lumber, and a free orientation. Beyond shop access, WorkbenchRVA offers woodworking classes, kids workshops, tool-basics sessions, and private one-on-one instruction — all open to non-members. A retail area stocks hardwoods, softwoods, exotic woods, sandpaper, and finishes. The company also accepts custom woodworking commissions for homes and businesses.

The shop serves hobbyists, beginners, weekend warriors, and families seeking creative outlets, as well as small businesses needing custom woodwork. Classes and kids programs are designed for participants without prior experience, emphasizing a welcoming, grade-free environment.

Dalton started WorkbenchRVA to give people — especially children — the space, tools, and instruction that schools no longer provide. The goal is to foster creativity and hands-on learning in a fun, supportive community setting.

about:
Worldpac Inc, headquartered in Woodlawn, Maryland, has been serving professional independent automotive service centers since 1969. The company operates as a wholesale distributor of original equipment (OE) automotive replacement parts, importing directly from manufacturers rather than producing its own components. No founders are named in public records, and ownership details such as family or veteran status are not disclosed.

Worldpac’s catalog encompasses more than 110,000 stocked products (over 120,000 by some counts) covering 41-plus vehicle carlines and 11 million-plus applications. Its proprietary speedDIAL online platform provides real-time availability, pricing, detailed images, and self-service ordering and returns for independent shops. Beyond parts distribution, the company offers carline-specific technical training, business management programs (branded Smart Groups), and turnkey marketing solutions designed to help shop owners focus on operations. Private-label brands include WORLD SOURCEONE AGM batteries, World Brake Resources brake pads, and METRIX climate-control components.

The primary customers are independent automotive repair facilities across North America, ranging from single-bay shops to multi-location operations. Worldpac positions itself as a partner that delivers the same breadth of OE parts and technical support traditionally available only to franchised dealers, enabling independents to service a wide mix of import and domestic vehicles.

Worldpac emphasizes its direct-from-manufacturer sourcing model and the depth of its digital catalog as key differentiators, claiming the largest import and domestic selection in North America and the industry’s most widely used electronic ordering system.

The company manufactures a range of dry and liquid products for the foodservice industry, including chicken breadings and batters, marinades and dips, all-natural and conventional seasoning blends, and fryer maintenance chemicals such as Filter Fresh and Fryer Fresh. Primary customers are foodservice operators, from independent fried-chicken restaurants to larger institutional kitchens that run prepared chicken programs. The firm positions itself as a consultative partner, offering operational expertise alongside its product line to help clients maximize yield and consistency.

Wynn's emphasizes its family heritage and time-tested formulations as differentiators, stating that its blends are crafted to please discerning palates and that its consultative approach extends beyond simple supply to include fryer management support and program development.

name: Xtreme Manufacturing
old_description: Founded in 2003, Xtreme Manufacturing has grown to become one of the leading manufacturers of telehandlers in North America, with an increasing global customer base.
about:
Xtreme Manufacturing is headquartered in Henderson, Nevada. Founded in 2003 by Don Ahern, the company originated from his dissatisfaction with telehandlers available for his rental fleet. After purchasing Western Attachments Company in 1999, an Oregon-based forklift maker, Ahern rebranded it as Xtreme Manufacturing in 2003 and relocated to Nevada.

The company designs and manufactures rough-terrain telescopic handlers (telehandlers) with 24 models spanning lifting capacities from 5,900 to 100,000 pounds and maximum lift heights up to 100 feet. It also produces Xtreme Cubes, a line of portable modular buildings for commercial, residential, and temporary uses. All assembly and engineering operations are conducted at its Henderson facility.

Xtreme serves construction, industrial, oil-and-gas, mining, and rental markets, as well as customers needing modular structures for offices, retail, workforce housing, restaurants, and trade-show booths.

Ahern started the business to build a more reliable telehandler using high-quality components that lower total cost of ownership. The company emphasizes features such as boom rollers instead of wear pads, 360-degree cab visibility, intuitive one-hand controls, and an integrated boom lift point. It backs products with a 10-year/5-year/2-year warranty and notes that all units are built in North America.

about:
A&H Manufacturing Worldwide, based in Johnston, Rhode Island, traces its roots to 1967 when jewelry salesman H. Jack Feibelman invented the hanging jewelry card, a design that became an industry standard. The company remained under Feibelman family leadership until 2022, when ownership transitioned to the Calandrelli family—Anthony and Daniel Calandrelli—who bring decades of packaging experience and continue the founder's legacy of customer-focused innovation.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures custom product packaging across four facilities worldwide. Its capabilities span carding, hang tags and tickets, boxes, labels, e-commerce packaging, molded specialty items, gift packaging, eco-friendly solutions, puff pads, and pouches. In-house design, engineering, and research teams handle projects from concept through production and delivery, serving both large retailers and smaller brands.

A&H serves a diverse client base that includes the world's largest retailers as well as businesses in jewelry, apparel, accessories, tools, hardware, and wine. The firm's packaging solutions are tailored to each product category, with an emphasis on brand storytelling and functional fit.

Feibelman's original insight—"When you can't find what you're looking for, you invent it"—still drives the company's approach. A&H differentiates itself through Made-in-USA production that reduces transportation emissions, a sustainability program that re-engineers packages to use less material, and a customer service model built on timely communication and creative problem-solving.

about:
ACI Plastics South, LLC runs a post-industrial plastics reprocessing plant in Liberty, South Carolina. The company focuses on converting plastic scrap into reusable resins and compounds for automotive and industrial supply chains.

The facility provides size reduction, multi-layer separation, electrostatic and density separation, fiber and optical sorting, patented paint removal, compounding on twin- and single-screw extruders, blending, pelletizing, and full logistics. Annual capacities include 70 million pounds of size reduction, 35 million pounds of separation, 10 million pounds of paint removal, and 40 million pounds of compounding. Equipment includes nine grinders, two shredders, two multi-layer separators, an electrostatic separator, a density separator, a fiber separator, an optical sorter, six paint-removal tanks, three twin-screw extruders, one single-screw extruder, multiple ribbon and paddle blenders, and a dedicated fleet of five tractors with 20 box trailers and two bulk trailers.

Primary customers are automotive manufacturers and tier suppliers generating multi-layer instrument panels, door panels, and painted TPO, PP, ABS, and PC/ABS parts. The company also serves broader post-industrial plastic waste streams, offering closed-loop programs that return reprocessed pellets or certified compounds to the original molder.

ACI Plastics differentiates itself with a patented paint-removal process that meets Class A surface requirements, a commercialized multi-layer separation technology achieving over 99.98% purity, an A2LA-accredited lab certified to ISO 17025:2017, and a logistics operation that handles pickup and delivery. The firm states its closed-loop model reduces material cost below virgin resin pricing.

about:
ADI Inc. is a family-owned wire and cable business based in Chanute, Kansas. The company was founded in 1990 by Merrill Cunningham after he left a corporate role to purchase the distribution side of an existing operation. Cunningham and his wife, Wendy, ran the business together for years before passing leadership to their sons, Scott and Stuart Cunningham, who now serve as CEO and plant manager, respectively. The second generation also includes Scott’s wife, Staci, in accounting, and Stuart’s wife, Becca, as office manager.

The company operates as both a value-added distributor of electrical wire, cable, and related products and a manufacturer of custom electrical harnesses and battery cable assemblies. ADI also maintains a UL-certified respooling operation (E146138) and offers dyeing, printing, and custom packaging services. The harness department has driven the firm’s most significant growth in recent years.

ADI serves customers worldwide, shipping throughout the United States and internationally. Its client base includes buyers who need exact cut lengths — such as 653 feet rather than standard 500- or 1,000-foot spools — as well as original equipment manufacturers and industrial users requiring custom wire harnesses, battery cables, and bonded or striped wire products. The company’s willingness to accommodate non-standard quantities and custom configurations has underpinned relationships spanning more than two decades.

Cunningham started the business to run his own operation after a corporate career, and the company’s differentiation rests on personalized service, flexible order quantities, and the ability to deliver locally within a 150-mile radius. The family-owned structure is cited as a reason for the personal care and responsiveness that the firm emphasizes.

AFL manufactures a full range of fiber optic cables, including OPGW (AlumaCore, CentraCore, HexaCore), ADSS (standard, mini‑span, flat drop, aerial drop), high‑density premise cables (MicroCore, armored tight‑buffered, hybrid fiber/copper), and harsh‑environment cables for subsea, downhole, and LSZH sensing applications. All cables are made to order, and AFL’s engineering team customizes designs for each application, supported by on‑site training and installation oversight. Primary markets include electric utilities (transmission and distribution), broadband and telecommunications, enterprise and data‑center networks, industrial facilities, hyperscale data centers, and subsea/refinery operations.

AFL emphasizes environmental stewardship: its cable plants are ISO 14001 certified, recycling rates for paper, wood, metal, and plastic exceed 85 percent, and a returnable steel‑reel program reduces waste. Its differentiator is the proactive monitoring layer, which aims to detect, diagnose, and resolve issues — often without rolling a truck — reducing downtime for end users.

AVID Racing operates from Fresno, California, where it designs, engineers, and manufactures its UTV suspension systems and titanium hardware under one roof.

The company produces platform-specific suspension kits, titanium hardware replacement packages, shocks, and builder components for side-by-side vehicles. Materials used are 7075 aluminum, 4130 chromoly, and Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy, selected per application. Manufacturing processes include precision machining, welding, and assembly, with fitment verified through an online Shock Center that matches specifications to vehicle configurations.

AVID serves the off-road powersports market, targeting UTV owners, racers, and fabricators who need direct-fit suspension upgrades and corrosion-resistant hardware. Concrete applications span Can-Am Maverick R and X3, Polaris RZR Pro R, and Yamaha YXZ1000 platforms, with kits ranging from 12-piece shock bolt sets to 170-piece ultimate suspension replacement packages.

The company differentiates itself through a geometry-first engineering approach that evaluates motion ratio, leverage curves, load paths, and steering behavior as an integrated system rather than maximizing travel alone. It promotes race-proven materials, in-house manufacturing control, and direct technical support without intermediaries.

AZ CAP Co, based in Prescott Valley, Arizona, traces its roots to 1999 when Arizona Cap & Apparel began as a small embroidery operation. The business was later taken over by Eva Janckila and Vance, who expanded its capabilities beyond embroidery into a full-service branding partner for apparel, promotional products, and print.

Today the company provides corporate apparel, headwear, promotional merchandise, signage, and print services from its Prescott Valley facility. Decoration processes include embroidery, screen printing, and direct-to-film (DTF) printing, with full all-over print capability for custom designs. The firm also manages factory-direct custom apparel programs and scalable fulfillment ranging from 25 to 25,000-plus units per order, offering more than 1,000 stocked product options.

Clients span automotive, insurance, event and concert promotion, construction contractors, retail, nonprofits, and financial services. National accounts such as Wells Fargo and PetSmart are referenced alongside marketing, human-resources, and operations teams that rely on the company for uniform programs, executive gifting, safety wear, and branded marketing essentials.

AZ CAP Co emphasizes a consultative approach built on clear communication, in-house expertise, and a vetted supplier network. Its stated differentiators include a 10-day average turnaround for decorated apparel, a sub-1% defect rate, 100% customer-approved designs before production, and 95% of orders completed within 14 business days. The mission is to simplify branded solutions so organizations can show up on brand and on schedule.

about:
Aaron Smith Industries is a family-owned fabrication shop based in Eagle Creek, Oregon, just outside Portland. The company operates from a facility on SE Highway 224 and emphasizes high-quality materials and equipment.

The shop provides custom fabrication across metal, wood, plastic, and foam. Core processes include certified TIG, MIG, and ARC welding with mobile service; cutting via CNC router, laser, plasma, sawing, and light-gauge metal shearing; sheet metal and pipe forming; sand blasting; and finishes such as powder coating, painting, and wood staining. Design work is handled in-house using V-Carve, Laserworks V8, SketchUp, and Adobe software. The equipment roster features a Smart Shop CNC router, CNC router table, laser cutter/engraver, plasma cutter, saws, and a light-gauge shear.

Aaron Smith Industries serves customers needing signage, custom woodworking, metal fabrication, rapid prototyping, artistic sculpture, jewelry, awards, memorials, and theme-park elements. Past projects cited by the company include 3D model making, sign making, wood carving, CNC routing, engraving, milling, new product designs, custom fireplaces, door panels, statues, jewelry, stone cutting, 3D sculptures, earrings, gifts, personalized awards, memorials, and commemorative plaques.

The company states its differentiation lies in quality, honesty, and speed—"Today it is rare to find quality, honesty and speed. Especially all in the same business," reads one testimonial. Aaron Smith Industries says it uses only high-quality materials and top-of-the-line equipment, maintains precise layout and attention to detail, and aims for efficient turnaround without sacrificing quality, backed by a commitment to 100% customer satisfaction.

about:
Founded in 2018 in Covington, Georgia, Absolics Inc. is a semiconductor packaging company backed by South Korea's SK Group. The venture began under the leadership of CEO Jiho Kang with a mission to redefine computing foundations using glass substrates after silicon hit a physical scaling wall.

The company develops glass substrate platforms for next-generation semiconductor packaging, targeting AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. Its SVM facility in Covington serves as a test and manufacturing ground for high-density packaging. With a team of 16, Absolics operates globally from offices in London and Singapore, supported by $75 million in CHIPS Act manufacturing subsidies and $100 million in R&D funding.

Absolics serves the semiconductor industry, particularly companies advancing AI accelerators, high-performance computing processors, and advanced packaging solutions.

The company was started to overcome the physical scaling limits of silicon by using glass as a substrate material, offering better thermal dissipation and signal integrity for high-density packaging.
